column1: Correct the sentence: "I am happy to meeting you."
column2: I am happy to meet you. Here "to" belongs to the infinitive, so the base verb follows.

column1: Correct the sentence: "I look forward to meet you."
column2: I look forward to meeting you. "To" is a preposition here, so a gerund (-ing) follows.

column1: How can a prepositional "to" be distinguished from an infinitive "to"?
column2: Replace the -ing form with "it" or "this". "I look forward to it" is valid, so "to" is a preposition and takes a gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "I look forward to ___ (see) you soon."
column2: seeing. Look forward to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "She is used to ___ (work) night shifts."
column2: working. Be used to + gerund means "accustomed to".

column1: What is the difference between "I used to work" and "I am used to working"?
column2: "Used to + base verb" describes a past habit that has ended. "Be used to + gerund" describes familiarity with something.

column1: Complete: "He is getting used to ___ (drive) on the left."
column2: driving. Get used to + gerund describes the process of becoming accustomed.

column1: Complete: "They are accustomed to ___ (wake) early."
column2: waking. Be accustomed to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "She objected to ___ (pay) the extra fee."
column2: paying. Object to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "He admitted to ___ (take) the document."
column2: taking. Admit to + gerund (admit alone may also take a gerund without "to").

column1: Complete: "She confessed to ___ (lie) about the results."
column2: lying. Confess to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "The team is committed to ___ (deliver) on time."
column2: delivering. Be committed to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "The course is dedicated to ___ (teach) advanced techniques."
column2: teaching. Be dedicated to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "She devoted herself to ___ (study) physics."
column2: studying. Devote oneself to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "Exercise contributes to ___ (improve) sleep quality."
column2: improving. Contribute to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "The company resorted to ___ (cut) salaries."
column2: cutting. Resort to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "Users must adapt to ___ (use) the new interface."
column2: using. Adapt to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "It took a week to adjust to ___ (live) abroad."
column2: living. Adjust to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "In addition to ___ (write) code, she reviews pull requests."
column2: writing. In addition to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "He sent the draft with a view to ___ (publish) it."
column2: publishing. With a view to + gerund.

column1: Complete: "Many users are opposed to ___ (pay) for updates."
column2: paying. Be opposed to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "She is addicted to ___ (check) her phone."
column2: checking. Be addicted to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "He is prone to ___ (forget) deadlines."
column2: forgetting. Be prone to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "The key to ___ (learn) a language is repetition."
column2: learning. Key to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "An alternative to ___ (use) paper is a tablet."
column2: using. Alternative to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "Poor planning can lead to ___ (miss) the deadline."
column2: missing. Lead to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "The total amounts to ___ (spend) 200 euros."
column2: spending. Amount to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "I am looking forward to ___ (hear) from you."
column2: hearing. Look forward to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "She stuck to ___ (follow) the original plan."
column2: following. Stick to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "The method is similar to ___ (use) a spreadsheet."
column2: using. Similar to + gerund or noun.

column1: Complete: "She is not accustomed to ___ (be) interrupted."
column2: being. Be accustomed to + gerund (passive: being + past participle).

column1: Complete: "We are close to ___ (finish) the project."
column2: finishing. Close to + gerund or noun.
